description: Experience the authentic flavors of India with this mouth-watering Tandoori Chicken, perfectly cooked over charcoal. The tender chicken pieces are marinated in a rich, spicy yogurt mixture, then grilled to smoky perfection. This recipe delivers a vibrant, aromatic dish that is a true delight for any dinner.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Make deep gashes all over the chicken pieces with a sharp knife. This helps the marinade penetrate deeply for maximum flavor. Set aside.

instructions.title: First Marinade Application
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and 1 teaspoon salt. Rub this mixture generously all over the chicken pieces, ensuring it gets into the gashes. Let it rest for 15-20 minutes at room temperature.

instructions.title: Prepare the Second Marinade
instructions.text: In another bowl, whisk together the thick yogurt, remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, remaining 0.5 teaspoon salt, black pepper powder, mustard oil, and optional red food color. Mix until a smooth, well-combined paste forms.

instructions.title: Second Marinade and Marination
instructions.text: Add the chicken pieces to the yogurt-spice mixture. Ensure each piece is thoroughly coated with the marinade. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight for best results. The longer the marination, the more tender and flavorful the chicken will be.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal to create medium-high heat. The coals should be glowing red with a light layer of ash. Ensure the grill grates are clean and lightly oiled to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly on the hot grill grates or thread them onto skewers if you have them. Grill for 25-35 minutes, turning occasionally to ensure even cooking and charring on all sides. During the last 10 minutes, baste the chicken with melted butter or oil to keep it moist and enhance flavor.

instructions.title: Check for Doneness and Serve
instructions.text: The chicken is cooked when its internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) and the juices run clear. It should have a beautiful reddish-brown color with slightly charred edges. Remove from the grill, let it rest for a few minutes, then garnish with fresh cilantro and lemon wedges. Serve hot.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, use a good quality hung curd or Greek yogurt as its thickness helps the marinade cling better to the chicken.
Do not skip the deep gashes on the chicken pieces; they are crucial for allowing the marinade to penetrate and flavor the meat from within.
Always let your grilled chicken rest for 5-10 minutes after cooking. This allows the juices to redistribute, resulting in more tender and succulent meat.
article:
Discover the tantalizing aroma and vibrant flavors of homemade Tandoori Chicken, a quintessential Indian dinner recipe that promises to transport your taste buds straight to the streets of Delhi or the finest Indian restaurants. While traditionally cooked in a scorching hot clay oven called a tandoor, we’re bringing that authentic smoky magic right to your backyard with a charcoal grill. Imagine tender, succulent chicken pieces, deeply marinated in a spiced yogurt blend, kissed by flames, and emerging with a beautiful char and an irresistible aroma. This article is your ultimate guide to mastering the classic Tandoori Chicken Recipe, ensuring a memorable meal that’s both engaging to prepare and a delight to devour. Get ready to impress your family and friends with this smoky, spicy, and utterly delicious Indian culinary masterpiece.

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?

Tandoori Chicken is an iconic South Asian dish, originating from the Punjab region of undivided India. Its name is derived from the "tandoor," a cylindrical clay oven used for cooking and baking. The dish is characterized by chicken marinated in yogurt and a blend of spices, then traditionally cooked at high temperatures within the tandoor. The intense heat cooks the chicken rapidly, sealing in juices while creating a distinct smoky flavor and a slightly charred exterior. The vibrant reddish-orange hue, often associated with Tandoori Chicken, comes from either Kashmiri red chili powder (which provides color without excessive heat) or, in some cases, a touch of food coloring.

When prepared on a charcoal grill, we aim to replicate the tandoor's unique cooking environment as closely as possible. The charcoal provides the intense, radiant heat necessary for quick cooking and, crucially, imparts that irreplaceable smoky flavor that is central to authentic Tandoori Chicken. Unlike a conventional oven, a charcoal grill allows for direct exposure to flame and smoke, developing a beautiful char and a depth of flavor that a tandoor would typically provide. This particular Tandoori Chicken Recipe focuses on the charcoal grilled method, ensuring a deeply flavorful and aromatic Indian dinner experience.

## Ingredients You Need for Tandoori Chicken

Gathering the right ingredients is the first step to a successful Tandoori Chicken Recipe. Quality ingredients make all the difference in flavor.

For the Chicken:
*   2-3 lbs chicken pieces (drumsticks, thighs, or a whole chicken cut into 8 pieces). Skin on or off is a preference, but skin on can help retain moisture and crisp up.
*   Lemon wedges and fresh cilantro for garnish.

For the First Marinade:
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste (freshly made is best)
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1/4 teaspoon red chili powder (or cayenne)

For the Second Marinade:
*   1 cup full-fat plain yogurt (Greek yogurt works well for its thickness)
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 tablespoon Kashmiri red chili powder (for color and mild heat)
*   1 teaspoon regular red chili powder (adjust to your spice preference)
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
*   1 teaspoon salt (or to taste)
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice
*   1 tablespoon mustard oil or vegetable oil (mustard oil adds an authentic pungent note)
*   Optional: 1/4 teaspoon red food coloring (for traditional vibrant color)

For Basting:
*   2 tablespoons melted butter or oil

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken

Creating this delicious Tandoori Chicken Recipe at home is a rewarding process. Follow these steps for an unforgettable meal:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make 2-3 deep slits into each chicken piece, especially on thicker parts. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply, ensuring maximum flavor and even cooking.

2.  **First Marinade (Acidic):** In a large bowl, combine the ingredients for the first marinade: 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon red chili powder. Rub this mixture all over the chicken pieces, ensuring it gets into the slits. Let it sit for 15-20 minutes at room temperature. This initial marinade tenderizes the chicken and helps the second marinade adhere better.

3.  **Second Marinade (Yogurt & Spices):** While the first marinade is working, prepare the second. In a separate bowl, whisk together the yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, Kashmiri red chili powder, regular red chili powder, cumin, coriander, garam masala, black pepper, salt, lemon juice, mustard oil (or vegetable oil), and the optional red food coloring. Ensure the mixture is smooth and well combined.

4.  **Combine Marinades:** Add the second marinade to the chicken, ensuring every piece is thoroughly coated. Use your hands to really work the marinade into the chicken and the slits. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, or ideally overnight (12-24 hours) for the best flavor and tenderness. The longer the marination, the better the results for your Tandoori Chicken Recipe.

5.  **Prepare the Charcoal Grill:** About 30-40 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal for two-zone cooking: pile charcoal on one side for direct, high heat, and leave the other side empty for indirect, medium heat. Aim for a medium-high temperature (around 375-400°F or 190-200°C). Clean your grill grates and oil them well to prevent sticking.

6.  **Grill the Chicken:**
    *   **Sear:** Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot charcoal (direct heat zone). Sear for 2-3 minutes per side to get a nice char and color.
    *   **Indirect Cooking:** Once seared, move the chicken to the indirect heat zone. Cover the grill and cook for 20-30 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) at its thickest part, without touching the bone. Flip and baste the chicken with melted butter or oil every 5-7 minutes to keep it moist and enhance flavor.
    *   **Final Char (Optional):** If desired, you can briefly move the chicken back over direct heat for another minute or two per side at the very end to enhance the char, being careful not to burn it.

7.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring moist and tender chicken. Garnish with fresh cilantro and lemon wedges before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Tandoori Chicken Results

Achieving restaurant-quality Tandoori Chicken at home is entirely possible with a few expert tips:

*   **Score Deeply:** Don't skimp on scoring the chicken. Deep cuts ensure the marinade penetrates to the bone, infusing flavor and promoting even cooking.
*   **Drain Your Yogurt:** If using regular plain yogurt, strain it through a cheesecloth for an hour or two to remove excess whey. This creates a thicker marinade that clings better to the chicken.
*   **Marination Time is Key:** The longer you marinate, the more tender and flavorful your chicken will be. Overnight is highly recommended for this Tandoori Chicken Recipe.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill:** Cook in batches if necessary. Overcrowding lowers grill temperature and steams the chicken instead of grilling it, preventing a good char.
*   **Monitor Heat:** Use a meat thermometer to ensure the chicken is cooked through (165°F/74°C) but not overcooked, which can dry it out.
*   **Baste Regularly:** Basting with butter or oil during the indirect cooking phase adds flavor, moisture, and helps develop a beautiful crust.
*   **Use Quality Spices:** Freshly ground or high-quality whole spices make a significant difference in the final taste of your Tandoori Chicken.

## Serving Suggestions for Tandoori Chicken

Tandoori Chicken is a star on its own, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Indian accompaniments. Here are some serving suggestions to complete your Indian dinner:

*   **Bread:** Serve with warm, fluffy naan bread, roti, or paratha to soak up all the delicious juices and spices.
*   **Chutney & Raita:** A cooling mint chutney or a refreshing cucumber raita (yogurt dip) provides a perfect counterpoint to the chicken's spice.
*   **Onions & Lemon:** Simple sliced red onions and extra lemon wedges are essential. The acidity of the lemon brightens the flavors, and the raw onion adds a delightful crunch.
*   **Rice:** A side of plain basmati rice or jeera rice (cumin rice) can be a comforting addition.
*   **Salad:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with a lemon dressing) adds freshness.
*   **Vegetables:** Grilled vegetables like bell peppers, onions, or zucchini, marinated in a similar spice blend, can be cooked alongside the chicken.

## Variations and Substitutions

This versatile Tandoori Chicken Recipe can be adapted to suit different preferences and dietary needs:

*   **Vegetarian Options:** For a vegetarian version, substitute chicken with large cubes of paneer (Indian cottage cheese), mushrooms, cauliflower florets, or thick slices of bell peppers. Marinate and grill similarly, adjusting cooking times.
*   **Other Meats:** This marinade works wonderfully with other meats like lamb chops, fish fillets (reduce marination time significantly for fish), or even large prawns.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder (both Kashmiri and regular) to suit your heat preference. For less heat, reduce the regular chili powder; for more, increase it.
*   **Dairy-Free:** For a dairy-free option, use a plant-based yogurt (like coconut or almond yogurt, ensuring it's unsweetened) or skip the yogurt and use extra lemon juice, vinegar, and a touch of oil to form a paste with the spices. The texture will be different, but the flavor can still be excellent.
*   **Alternative Cooking Methods:** While charcoal grilling is highly recommended for the authentic smoky flavor, you can also make Tandoori Chicken in a conventional oven (broil on high, turning frequently), on a gas grill (aim for high heat), or even in an air fryer (at 375°F/190°C, flipping halfway). However, the charcoal grill truly delivers the most authentic taste for this Indian dinner recipe.

Embrace the joy of cooking this classic Tandoori Chicken Recipe right in your own home. The effort is minimal for the incredible burst of flavor you'll experience. The smoky char from the charcoal grill, combined with the deeply aromatic marinade, creates a dish that is truly unforgettable. So fire up your grill, gather your ingredients, and embark on this culinary adventure to delight in the rich flavors of this timeless Indian dinner recipe. Enjoy every succulent bite!
